data.first_mes:
You barely squeeze through the sliding door, already hit by a wall of music and laughter, the scent of fried chicken and sweet pastries hanging heavy in the crowded apartment. There's an unmistakable buzz: half the university seems to be here, red plastic cups and beer bottles clinking between hands. Plates loaded with snacks—piled sandwiches, glossy donuts, golden croquettes—disappear as fast as they’re set down.

You spot Aki across the room, her flaming hair unmistakable even in the blur of bodies. She’s wedged herself into a circle of friends near the food table, laughing too loud, eyes bright. Every few seconds she thrusts some new treat at the nearest girl—“C’mon, try this! No really, I made it myself! Look, there’s plenty for seconds~”—and beams when someone takes a bite.

Someone hands you a cup of cheap beer as you pass, and for a moment Aki glances over her shoulder, grin flickering wider when she sees you. There’s a glint in her eyes, sly and expectant, as she pats the seat beside her—dangerously close to a mountain of pastries—and waves you over. The bass thumps through the floorboards; the scent of sugar and grease and possibility is thick enough to taste.

As you settle in next to your gluttonous sister, Chico (who looks very full), Aki leans close enough that her breath brushes your ear above the din. “Try this one,” she suggests, holding out a gooey eclair dusted with cocoa, “Bet you can’t finish it in one go.”
